coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Room
That Feels Too Quiet
coverDek: For the empty apartment, the phone that doesn't ring, and the ache of being surrounded by people yet still feeling unseen.

points.hook: Lord, You counted the stars by name before You ever counted my friends.
paragraphs: Loneliness isn't proof You forgot me — it's proof I'm human, built for connection, aching exactly the way a soul aches when it's missing what it was made for. So before I ask You to fill the room, let me just tell You it's empty tonight, and let that honesty be enough of a prayer for today.
points.verseText: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.

points.hook: I declare: empty is not the same as forsaken.
paragraphs: I refuse to let an empty chair at my table talk me into believing an empty promise from my God. He said He would never leave me nor forsake me, and I stand on that louder than I feel it today — because faith was never about matching your feelings, it's about outlasting them.
points.verseText: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

points.hook: Your body isn't lying to you when it feels this heavy in an empty room.
paragraphs: I know the specific ache of loneliness — a quiet apartment that somehow feels louder than noise, a tight chest from scrolling past gatherings you weren't invited to. I'm not asking you to perform fine. I'm asking you to notice the ache, breathe through it, and let Me sit in the quiet with you before you try to fix it or explain it away.
points.verseText: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

points.hook: You were never designed to carry this alone — and neither was I.
paragraphs: Somebody reading this right now needs to hear it from someone, not just something: you belong to a body, not just a feed. Reach out today — a call, a text, a seat saved at a table — because God's usual way of answering a lonely prayer is to send a person, and sometimes that person is you, sent to somebody lonelier than you knew.
points.verseText: Two are better than one... for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.

points.hook: Come sit with Me a while, child — you don't have to perform okay in this room.
paragraphs: I see every meal you've eaten alone this month, every call that went to voicemail, every holiday you dreaded walking into solo. I'm not far off watching your loneliness from a distance — I'm present in the middle of it, closer than the silence itself, and I'm not leaving before the ache does. Rest in Me tonight. I've got the whole night shift.
points.verseText: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these found you tonight, don't let today be the day you go quiet again — reach out to someone, and let's stay connected too.
